sandy.notes: Low water-holding capacity; magnifies dry spell impact on high-water crops like maize.

loam.notes: Balanced soil texture with optimal water-holding capacity and aeration; neutral baseline.

clay.notes: High water retention buffers against short dry spells, but presents waterlogging risk under heavy rains.

unknown.notes: Texture unknown; no modifier applied, lowers data confidence.

poor.notes: Prone to seasonal saturation; penalizes crops sensitive to waterlogging (maize, groundnut).

moderate.notes: Standard field drainage with minimal saturation risk.

well.notes: Rapid infiltration; minimizes standing water but may require higher organic matter to retain moisture.

unknown.notes: Drainage status unknown; flags need for local soil assessment.

low.notes: Degraded soil structure; increases priority for residue-building and nitrogen-fixing crops.

medium.notes: Moderate baseline fertility typical of savanna croplands.

high.notes: High organic matter provides moisture buffering and soil microbial activity.

unknown.notes: Organic matter level unmeasured; lowers data confidence.

rain_fed.notes: Fully dependent on NASA POWER rainfall timing and quantity.

limited_irrigation.notes: Supplemental irrigation available during critical flowering dry spells.

irrigated.notes: Full irrigation system; water fit criteria decoupled from seasonal dry spells.

flat.notes: Minimal runoff velocity; lower erosion risk.

gentle.notes: Standard undulating savanna topography; standard erosion risk.

steep.notes: High runoff and topsoil loss risk; heavily weights ground cover traits.

unknown.notes: Field slope unmeasured; neutral weighting with documented information gap.
